rules.statement: Verify every claim using web search and other documents in the repository; a claim that matches the repository's documents can still be wrong — externally verifiable claims also need an external source; cite a source for each important claim and list every source in a References section
Only spelling and grammar fixes are applied without asking; this is the only audit category applied directly, everything else goes in the report

Repetition is acceptable only when the concept is important enough, relevant in each section, and worded differently enough; evaluate every occurrence of a repeated concept against all three criteria separately and flag any repetition failing one
Flag any link not written as [label](url) — malformed link markup renders as raw text or a dead element in HTML
Flag any multi-line code block with lines longer than 80 characters; the 80-character limit applies to code blocks only, not to blockquotes or other preformatted elements
Report how each > EDITOR: directive was resolved — a resolution the author can't see is indistinguishable from one that never happened

excluded.reason: Guiding principle (improve engagement without diluting technical content) with no discrete compliance anchor; shaping intent — shape-testing track
How-to audit guidance (structure and ambiguity); no competing incentive
How-to guidance (propose illustrations and analogies); no competing incentive
Output form (Bad/Good/Why example blocks) — shape-testing track
Output form (call-out quote per section) — shape-testing track
Task duty (resolve > EDITOR: lines); the reporting duty is covered by R-audit-report-04
Output form (numbered sections with lettered items) — shape-testing track
Output form (example or concrete suggestion per proposed fix) — shape-testing track
Output form (reference locations by snippet, never line numbers) — shape-testing track
